abstract: For a primitive positive rational Collatz cycle, suppose its binary shortcut parity word is a unit-rotation coding by at most two cyclic intervals. We prove an explicit exponential lower bound for its common reduced denominator $q$: $q>2^{n/1643-11}/n^{16}$, where $n$ is the least shortcut period. A determinant-sensitive inequality precedes the classical power-separation input. The proof transfers Armstrong's integer-repetition and inverse-continued-fraction argument to shortcut blocks, combines it with the finite Denjoy–Koksma discrepancy bound and parity-cylinder packing, and eliminates the shared continued-fraction cost. Thus no separate bound on that cost or on discrepancy is required. The consequence $q=1$ forces $n<2^{19}$ within this coding family, without classifying arbitrary cycles or checking all smaller members. The contribution is the uniform denominator bound and its shortcut-clock coupling; the constituent discrepancy and repetition mechanisms are explicitly attributed. No numerical enumeration is a proof premise.
